system_overview: This specification models Dijkstra's algorithm for distributed termination detection on a ring, published as EWD 840: 'Derivation of a termination detection algorithm for distributed computations' by Dijkstra, Feijen, and van Gasteren (Information Processing Letters 16:217-219, 1983). The algorithm detects when all nodes in a ring have become inactive, using a token that circulates around the ring. Nodes and the token can be colored white or black to track whether messages have been sent against the direction of token flow.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring (numbered 0 through N-1) and a single token that circulates among them. Node 0 is the initiator that starts and evaluates token rounds. Each node can be active (computing) or passive, and each node has a color (white or black). The token also has a color and a position indicating which node currently holds it. The system is divided into two subsystems: the termination detection algorithm (System) that controls token passing, and the underlying computation (Environment) that models nodes sending messages and deactivating.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) the activation status of each node (active or passive), (2) the color of each node (white or black), (3) the current position of the token (which node holds it), and (4) the color of the token (white or black).
initial_state: The token is initially black. The activation status of nodes, node colors, and token position may take any type-correct values. This models an arbitrary starting state where the token's black color ensures no false termination detection.
actions: The algorithm defines the following actions: (1) Initiate probe: when node 0 holds the token and either node 0 is black or the token is black, it sends a white token to node N-1 and paints itself white. (2) Pass token: a non-zero node holding the token passes it to the next lower-numbered node if the node is inactive, or if the node or token is black (which will cause an inconclusive round). The token is stained black if the node is black; the node is then painted white. (3) Send message: an active node activates another node (simulating message delivery). If the activated node has a higher number than the sender, the sender paints itself black (since the message goes against token flow direction). (4) Deactivate: any active node may become inactive at any time.
safety_properties: The main safety property (termination detection) states that if the token is at node 0, the token is white, node 0 is white, and node 0 is inactive, then every node in the ring is inactive. Dijkstra's inductive invariant ensures this: either all nodes after the token position are inactive, or some node between 0 and the token position is black, or the token is black.
liveness_properties: If all nodes become inactive (termination occurs), then termination is eventually detected (the token arrives at node 0 in a white state with node 0 white and inactive).
model_bounds: The number of nodes N is declared as a constant positive natural number. For model checking, N must be instantiated with a specific finite value.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for the System actions (token passing and probe initiation), ensuring the termination detection mechanism makes progress. No fairness is assumed for the Environment actions. The algorithm implements a higher-level specification of synchronous termination detection in a ring.
